The WWTF is a fully enclosed facility (e.g., tanks, concrete-lined facilities of limited areal extent), which consists of an influent lift station and headworks, three primary clarifiers, three oxidation ditches, four secondary clarifiers, two primary digesters, one secondary digester, two centrifuges, and 15 evaporation/percolation ponds.
The oxidation ditches operate in parallel and provide biological treatment where aerobic and anoxic zones provide nitrification and denitrification for nitrogen removal.

The WWTF is a fully enclosed facility (e.g., tanks, concrete-lined facilities of limited areal extent), which consists of an influent lift station and headworks, three primary clarifiers, three oxidation ditches, four secondary clarifiers, two primary digesters, one secondary digester, two centrifuges, and 15 evaporation/percolation ponds.
According to the 2019 RWD, current sludge handling operations at the WWTF consist of transferring sludge from the two primary digesters to a secondary anaerobic digester.
Treated sludge is then dewatered using two skid mounted centrifuges, after which the dewatered cake is deposited into trailers which are hauled off by Synagro for composting.
The WWTF ... consists of ... 15 evaporation/percolation ponds. In the past, the Facility utilized 14 evaporation/percolation ponds for effluent disposal.

In addition, the Facility includes an unlined emergency disposal pond across a surface area of five acres. According to City staff, the emergency holding pond can be used to hold raw wastewater and/or primary effluent in the event of an emergency, if maintenance is required, or if the primary effluent pumps fail.
